\(W_d^*\) Power simulation figures and summary table for GitHub

Bashir Hamidi

2026-03-26

1 Preliminaries

1.1 Load packages

library(tidyverse); packageVersion("tidyverse")
## [1] '2.0.0'
library(ggplot2); packageVersion("ggplot2")
## [1] '4.0.2'
library(reshape2); packageVersion("reshape2")
## [1] '1.4.5'

1.2 Load data

df_raw <- df_raw %>% rename(., 
                                    "aWd*" = "p_value_adist",
                                    "t-test" = "p_value_t_test")
(df_working <- df_raw)

1.3 Output directory

1.4 Simulation scenario

\To look at Type I error: \X <-> M -> Y

\Y independent of X | M 
\Xi = 0 if 1<i<=n0; 1 if n0+1<i<=n0+n1 
\Mi ~ N(b*Xi, sd=1) 
\Yi ~ N(d*Mi, sd=1) = d*N(b*Xi, sd=1) + N(0,sd=1)

\X (exposure) -> M (mediator) 
\M -> R (response) (b) 
\X -> R (d = 0)

\To look at power 
\X <-> M -> Y <-

2 Summarizing data

signif = 0.05
   
df_sum  <- df_working %>% group_by(n0, n1, b, d, k) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(`Adjusted Wd*` = mean(`aWd*` < signif),
                    `t-test` = mean(`t-test` < signif))
## `summarise()` has regrouped the output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by n0, n1, b, d, and k.
## ℹ Output is grouped by n0, n1, b, and d.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.groups = "drop_last")` to silence this message.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.by = c(n0, n1, b, d, k))` for per-operation grouping
##   (`?dplyr::dplyr_by`) instead.
# We went from 12 million to 1,200, reducing by a factor of 10k which is the number of repetitions we did for each scenario. 

df_sum_melted <- reshape2::melt(df_sum,
                         id.vars = c("n0", "n1", "b", "d", "k"),
                         measure.vars = c("Adjusted Wd*", "t-test"),
                         variable.name = "Method",
                         value.name = "Reject")
# went from two cols to 1 col so doubled the nrow

df_sum_melted$n = 
  df_sum_melted$n0 + 
  df_sum_melted$n1

df_sum_melted
df_sum_melted$balance <- with(df_sum_melted, n0/n1)

3 Save summary table for GitHub

Raw table with 12 million observations (12M rows and 8 columns) is 422 MB, which is beyond the the limits for GitHub files.

We will preserve the raw data table in our records and share the summary table (12M/10k replicates = 1200 observations). This is more manageable for sharing on GitHub.

saveRDS(df_sum_melted, 
        file = paste0(output_dir, "Adjusted WdS_power simulation_summary table.rds"))

4 Figure 3

subset(Adjusted Wd*, b = 2) as row
x = n0
color = k
shape = n1
facets = d.b

chunk_plot_name <- "Figure 3"
chunk_plot <-
  ggplot(subset(df_sum_melted, Method == "Adjusted Wd*" & 
                  b %in% c(2) #& d %in% c(.5, 1)
                ),  
      aes(x=(n0), y=Reject, group=interaction(n1, k))) +
  geom_point(aes(color=factor(k), shape=factor(n1), stroke=.4), size=3, alpha=0.7) + 
  geom_line(aes(color=factor(k)), size=.5, alpha=0.8 ) + 
  #geom_point(aes(shape=factor(n1), color=factor(Method), fill=alpha("white", 0.2), size=3)) + 
  facet_grid(b~d, labeller=label_both)+ #d~b
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = expression(paste("Simulation with direct effect")))+ #Adjusted W[d]^{*}  #$W_d^*$
     ylab("Rejection Rate") + 
     xlab("n0 Sample Size")+
  theme(plot.background= element_rect(fill=NULL),
            legend.position="bottom",
            legend.byrow=TRUE,# whether the legend-matrix is filled by columns (FALSE, the default) or by rows (TRUE).
            legend.title=element_text(size=25),
            legend.text=element_text(size=25),
            text=element_text(size=25),  #size of xlab and ylab, also size of strip.text.y but but latter is changed by a ratio
            axis.text.x=element_text(size=13),  #grid/wrap tick label size
            axis.text.y=element_text(size=20)#, #grid/wrap tick label size
            ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(5, 10, 20, 50, 100), minor_breaks=NULL) +#+  #seq(-3,2,0.5)
  scale_shape_discrete(name="n1 Sample Size") +
  scale_color_discrete(name="Direct-Effect Multiplier") +
  guides(shape=guide_legend(title.position = "top", override.aes = list(size=4, stroke=1.4), order=2),
         color=guide_legend(title.position = "top", override.aes = list(size=4, stroke=1.4), order=1)
         ) 
## Warning: Using `size` aesthetic for lines was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0.
## ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead.
## This warning is displayed once per session.
## Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was
## generated.
png(paste0(output_dir, (chunk_plot_name),".png"), width=17, height=6, units="in", res=400)#, width=18, height=14)
print(chunk_plot)
dev.off()
## quartz_off_screen 
##                 2
print(chunk_plot)

5 Figure S2

5.1 S2 a

subset(k=1)

chunk_plot_name <- "Figure S2_A"
chunk_plot <-
  ggplot(subset(df_sum_melted, k == 1),  
      aes(x=(n0), y=Reject, group=interaction(n1, Method))) +
  geom_point(aes(color=(factor(n1)), shape=factor(Method), stroke=.4), size=3.5, alpha=0.4) + 
  geom_line(aes(color=(factor(n1))), size=.5, alpha=0.8 ) + 
  facet_grid(d~b, labeller=label_both)+ #d~b
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = expression(paste("A")),
       subtitle = "Simulation with direct effect, k=1") + 
  ylab("Rejection Rate") + 
  xlab("n0 Sample Size")+
  theme(plot.background= element_rect(fill=NULL),
            legend.position="bottom",
            legend.byrow=TRUE,# whether the legend-matrix is filled by columns (FALSE, the default) or by rows (TRUE).
            legend.title=element_text(size=25),
            plot.title=element_text(size=50),
            legend.text=element_text(size=25),
            text=element_text(size=25),  #size of xlab and ylab, also size of strip.text.y but but latter is changed by a ratio
            axis.text.x=element_text(size=10),  #grid/wrap tick label size
            axis.text.y=element_text(size=20)#, #grid/wrap tick label size
            ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(5, 10, 20, 50, 100), minor_breaks=NULL) +  #seq(-3,2,0.5)
  scale_color_discrete(name="n1 Sample Size") +
  scale_shape_discrete(name="Method") +
  guides(color=guide_legend(title.position = "top", override.aes = list(size=4, stroke=1.4), order=1),
         shape=guide_legend(title.position = "top", override.aes = list(size=4, stroke=1.4), order=2)) 
png(paste0(output_dir, (chunk_plot_name),".png"), width=12, height=12, units="in", res=400)
print(chunk_plot)
dev.off()
